high.title: Oil Prices Break $100 Again – Can Government Keep Inflation in 2% Range in H2?
high.summary:
International oil prices have surged sharply on renewed Middle East conflict tensions, posing a direct threat to South Korea's H2 inflation management target of 2%. According to the report, inflation is projected to breach 3% during August–September, prompting the government to heighten vigilance and mobilize a full-scale response. This development carries significant implications for KRW, Korean government bonds (KTBs), and Bank of Korea (BOK) monetary policy:

- **FX Impact:** A sustained oil price shock is structurally negative for KRW, as Korea is a major energy importer. Higher import costs widen the trade deficit, pressuring the current account and creating KRW depreciation headwinds.
- **Rates/Bonds:** If inflation overshoots to 3%+, the BOK's scope for further rate cuts becomes severely constrained or may be delayed, pressuring the front-end of the KTB curve. Bond investors should reassess duration risk.
- **Policy Watch:** The government's mobilization of an "all-response" framework signals political sensitivity. Watch for emergency fuel stabilization measures, oil tax cuts, or BOK communication shifts at the upcoming August MPC meeting.

*Key risk: A prolonged oil shock could force the BOK to hold rates higher for longer, flattening or inverting the short-end of the curve.*

---

high.title: USD-KRW Trades in Early 1,460s in New York Session
high.summary:
The USD-KRW exchange rate was trading at 1,461.80 won as of 9:18 PM during the New York session on July 24, representing a decline of 5.00 won from the prior session — a meaningful intraday KRW strengthening move. The pair had closed the Seoul regular session (approximately 3:30 PM KST) at 1,466.60 won, down just 0.20 won, suggesting that the bulk of the KRW appreciation came during the offshore/New York hours. This divergence between the onshore close and the New York session level is significant for FX traders, as it implies building momentum for a lower USD-KRW open in the next Seoul session.

The move into the low-1,460s suggests mild USD softness in the broader global FX market, likely driven by a combination of improved risk sentiment and potential USD weakening flows. Traders should monitor whether this offshore strength is sustained into the Seoul open, which could bring the pair closer to technical support in the 1,455–1,460 range. Any continued USD softness, particularly if Fed rate cut expectations firm up, could accelerate KRW gains. Watch for BOK commentary or any smoothing intervention if moves become disorderly.

---

medium.title: South Korea Financial Regulators Release Weekly Schedule (BOK, FSC, FSS – Week of July 27)
medium.summary: Several data releases next week are directly relevant to KRW and rates traders. Monday (July 28) brings **Resident Foreign Currency Deposit Trends for June 2026** — a key indicator of domestic FX demand and dollarization pressure. Tuesday (July 29) features the **Consumer Survey Results for July 2026**, which includes household inflation expectations critical to BOK's reaction function, alongside **Financial Institution Weighted Average Interest Rates for June 2026**, offering insight into pass-through from BOK policy to lending/deposit rates. The **Business Survey Index** on Thursday and the **Regional Economic Report** on Wednesday round out the macro picture. Traders should pay particular attention to consumer confidence and inflation expectation components, which could reinforce or soften the inflationary signal from the oil price surge noted above.

medium.title: Shinhan Securities Predicts Japan's Long-Term Rates to Peak in Q4 Amid Elevated Yields
medium.summary: Shinhan Investment Corp. analysts Ko Da-young and Kim Chan-hee project that Japan's 10-year JGB yields — currently near 30-year highs — will peak around Q4 2026, contingent on easing of external tightening concerns and resolution of key uncertainties. While this is a Japan-specific call, it has meaningful spillover implications for Korean markets: elevated JGB yields historically exert upward pressure on KTB yields via global duration repricing, and JPY weakness/strength dynamics directly influence KRW through regional FX correlations and export competitiveness. A Q4 peak scenario, if credible, may provide some relief to KTB long-end holders in 2027. Fund managers with cross-Asia fixed income exposure should monitor BOJ policy signals closely alongside this forecast.

medium.title: US July S&P PMI — Services Improves to 8-Month High, Manufacturing Slows to 4-Month Low
medium.summary: US July flash PMI data showed services activity jumping to 53.6 (from June's 51.2), an eight-month high, while manufacturing slipped to a four-month low at 53.8. The mixed reading — a resilient services sector offset by softer manufacturing — presents a nuanced picture for Fed policy expectations. For KRW and Korean bond traders, a still-solid US services sector could temper aggressive Fed easing bets, providing some floor for the USD and limiting KRW upside in the near term. However, the manufacturing softness may reinforce concerns about global industrial demand, which is directly relevant to Korea's export-heavy economy and current account trajectory. Bond investors should note that a resilient US economy could keep US Treasury yields elevated, exerting modest upward pressure on Korean government bond yields via the global rates channel.

medium.title: ECB Chief Economist: Current Situation 'Not a Red Alert' Requiring Swift Action
medium.summary: ECB Chief Economist Philip Lane characterized the current monetary environment — including elevated oil prices — as a "medium-sized shock," explicitly stating it does not rise to the level requiring urgent policy action as seen in 2022. Lane indicated the ECB is assessing the precise level of interest rates on a meeting-by-meeting basis. For KRW and Korean bond markets, a more measured and non-reactive ECB stance supports broader global risk sentiment, which is generally KRW-positive. It also signals that global rate volatility may remain contained for now, a constructive backdrop for Korean government bonds. Traders should monitor whether ECB caution aligns with any dovish pivot expectations that could weaken the EUR and indirectly support the USD.

medium.title: Trump Launches Section 301 Investigation Against EU Over Big Tech Fines, Threatens 'Substantial Tariffs'
medium.summary: President Trump announced a Section 301 trade investigation against the EU in retaliation for fines totaling tens of billions of dollars levied against US Big Tech firms including Apple, Meta, and Amazon, threatening "substantial tariffs." While this is primarily a US-EU trade dispute, it carries indirect relevance for Korean markets as an escalation in global trade tensions. Renewed tariff rhetoric tends to weigh on risk sentiment broadly, which can pressure EM currencies including the KRW. Korea, as a highly trade-dependent economy, is also sensitive to any signs of a broader global protectionist wave. KRW traders should watch for any risk-off spillover and monitor whether Trump's tariff threats extend beyond the EU to other trading partners.
